user_query: I need a lightweight image classification model that recognizes handwritten numbers. The model will run on a CPU-only system with 4 GB of RAM. It should aim for accuracy of at least 90%, use less than approximately 500 MB of runtime memory, and process an image within 200 milliseconds.
use_case_description: Lightweight image classification model for handwritten digits on a CPU-only system with 4 GB RAM; target accuracy >= 90%; runtime memory <= 500 MB; processing time <= 200 ms per image.

applicable_policies.guidance: Choose the largest hardware-safe micro-batch. For classification, use gradient accumulation only when needed to reach a moderate effective batch; effective_batch=batch_size*gradient_accumulation_steps*gpu_count. Never exceed training_hardware.max_batch_size. Preserve a grounded recipe optimizer by default. For Ultralytics optimizer='auto', do not claim control of learning_rate because Ultralytics derives and overrides it. A grounded recipe or a specifically justified LLM decision may instead select a supported explicit optimizer; in that case choose learning_rate jointly with effective batch size and treat linear batch scaling as a starting heuristic, not a mandatory formula.

Choose epochs from dataset size and transfer-learning mode. Smaller datasets may need more epochs but earlier stopping. Keep patience below num_epochs, warmup a small fraction of training, and leave enough post-warmup epochs for learning.

For pretrained models, prefer a short staged head warm-up only for small data (current train_images=12000, min_per_class=1200); otherwise fine-tune all layers. High domain shift, when explicitly known, favors immediate unfreezing. A positive freeze duration requires training_mode='staged_fine_tune' and must be shorter than num_epochs.
Use macro_f1 for materially imbalanced multiclass data (current imbalance_ratio=1.0); otherwise prefer val_acc unless the user explicitly prioritizes loss calibration.

Use conservative regularization for small datasets and stronger augmentation only with enough data. Avoid stacking strong label smoothing, MixUp, and CutMix. Preserve label semantics; when orientation/color/text safety is unknown, keep destructive transforms conservative.

Use warmup and optional gradient clipping for transformer-style or otherwise unstable full-model fine-tuning. Scheduler parameters must be consistent with num_epochs and learning_rate; cosine minimum LR must remain below the base LR.

model.description: A very lightweight CNN family designed for mobile/embedded use. MobileNetV3 small offers strong efficiency with good accuracy, making it a good fit for 28x28 MNIST style digits on CPU.

model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale:
Reasoning for the choice is driven by the provided constraints: CPU-only system with 4 GB RAM, runtime memory limit around 500 MB, and latency target of 200 ms per image, while needing at least 90 percent accuracy on MNIST style digits. MobileNetV3 Small is among the lightest architectures in the candidate set and tends to deliver solid accuracy with very low compute. The 28x28 MNIST input can be accommodated by using a 1-channel input (grayscale) or by converting to 3 channels with channel replication, which MobileNetV3 can handle with minor architectural adjustments. The small footprint helps keep both model size and runtime memory well under the 500 MB cap; the reduced compute keeps inference latency within the 200 ms budget on typical consumer CPUs. MNIST style digits are easy to classify with such a network, and accuracy well above 90% is achievable with proper training, data normalization, and optional quantization at inference time. If necessary, a minor shift to a slightly larger but still efficient variant (for example, MobileNetV2) can be used as a fallback, but MobileNetV3 Small is the strongest initial match for the stated constraints.

Notes on latency and feasibility:
- Measured latency: not provided in this context; the estimate is based on common benchmarks for MobileNetV3 Small on CPU with small inputs and single image inference. Expected range is roughly 60 to 150 ms per image on a typical consumer CPU, especially with 1x1 round trips and no heavy pre/post processing, and further reduced with 8-bit quantization.
- Unverified CPU feasibility: given the 4 GB RAM limit and a 1 image batch size, this architecture should be feasible within memory and time budgets when using standard optimizations (quantization, efficient runtime, and lightweight pre/post processing).
- Fallback: if latency or memory exceedance is observed in practice, switch to mobilenet_v2 with quantization or reduce input resolution/quality, and ensure 1-channel input to minimize compute. EfficientNet-B0 is generally heavier and should be a last resort if needs grow beyond current budgets.

dataset_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Selected 1,500 training samples per digit from the MNIST training split (mnist_cls_train) for each of the 10 classes. This yields a balanced per-class pool of 1,500 images, totaling 15,000 images across all classes. Rationale for this pool: (1) Domain alignment with handwritten digits (grayscale, 28x28) and image classification task; (2) Consistency within a single dataset family (MNIST) to maximize cross-class compatibility and reduce annotation-conversion issues; (3) Meets the target of ~1,500 images per class across train/validation/test, while staying well under the per-class cap of 10,000 and the overall cap of 50,000 images. The default budget is not limiting here since 15,000 total training images is far below the stated budgets. This pool should support training a lightweight model (e.g., MobileNetV3 Small) that can achieve the target accuracy on CPU with memory and latency constraints described. Note: official validation/test splits will be derived deterministically from this training pool; test/validation data may be used as external benchmarks if needed.

hyperparameter_decision_evidence.rationale: Configuration crafted to meet CPU-only deployment with <500 MB runtime memory and <=200 ms per image on a 28x28 MNIST-style task by using a very lightweight backbone (MobilenetV3 Small). Input images are resized to 224x224 and converted to 3-channel to align with pretrained weights. Transfer learning with a pretrained backbone is used to reach ≥90% accuracy on MNIST-like digits with reasonable training time on a consumer CPU. A cosine learning-rate schedule with a small warmup period supports gradual stabilization. A small batch size (4) is chosen to respect memory constraints; a non-zero momentum with SGD provides stable convergence. Regularization and augmentation are kept conservative to preserve digit semantics while enabling generalization. If latency or memory exceedances are observed, reduce input size or switch to quantized inference and/or a lighter augmentation strategy. Executable constraints applied: lora_rank=8 (LoRA rank is inactive outside LoRA training.); lora_alpha=16 (LoRA alpha is inactive outside LoRA training.); lora_dropout=0.05 (LoRA dropout is inactive outside LoRA training.); min_learning_rate=1e-06 (Cosine decay requires a non-negative floor below the base learning rate.); eps=1e-08 (The field is inactive for the selected optimizer or scheduler.); alpha=0.99 (The field is inactive for the selected optimizer or scheduler.) Added fallback rationales for: criterion_name, horizontal_flip_probability, model_name, momentum, nesterov, weight_decay.
